title: Gyeran Mari
subtitle: Korean rolled omelette with vegetables
excerpt: Gyeran mari is a Korean rolled egg omelette made with finely chopped spring onions and carrots. It serves 4 as a banchan side dish and takes 20 minutes. The egg is cooked in thin layers and rolled tightly in the pan to create neat slices with a spiral cross-section.
sourceNotes: Gyeran mari is a staple of the Korean dosirak, the packed lunchbox that is central to Korean food culture. It has been prepared in Korean homes and school kitchens for generations and is one of the first dishes many Korean children learn to cook. The technique of rolling eggs in a pan is also found in Japanese tamagoyaki, though the Korean version uses different seasonings and a rounder pan shape.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to 2 hours ahead and served at room temperature. Keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

glossaryTerms.definition: Gyeran mari means egg roll in Korean, from gyeran (egg) and mari (roll or wrap). It is a rolled omelette cooked in a frying pan and sliced into rounds to reveal a neat spiral. It is one of the most common components of the Korean dosirak lunchbox and appears regularly as a banchan side dish at home meals.

Banchan are the small side dishes served alongside rice at a Korean meal. They range from simple seasoned vegetables to fermented kimchi, braised tofu, and stir-fried anchovies. Several banchan are always present at once, and diners share them from the centre of the table. The number of banchan on a table traditionally reflected the wealth and generosity of the host.

content.text: is a rolled Korean omelette cooked in layers in a frying pan. The egg is seasoned simply and studded with fine pieces of spring onion and carrot, then rolled into a tight cylinder and sliced into rounds that show a clean spiral when cut.

Use a small frying pan, ideally 20cm, so the egg layer is thick enough to roll easily. Keep the heat low throughout. Pour the egg in small amounts, let it partially set, then use a spatula to fold and roll from one side to the other. If the egg sets before you roll it, it will crack. Work steadily and do not rush. A few drops of sesame oil in the egg mixture add flavour without overpowering.
Beat the eggs in a bowl with the salt and sesame oil until the yolks and whites are fully combined. Stir in the spring onions and carrots.
Heat a small 20cm frying pan over low to medium-low heat. Add the oil and swirl to coat.
Pour in about one-third of the egg mixture. Tilt the pan to spread it evenly. Cook until the egg is about 80 per cent set on the surface but still slightly wet on top.
Using a spatula, fold the near edge of the egg over towards the far edge, rolling it into a log shape. Slide the roll to the far side of the pan.

Pour another third of the egg mixture into the empty space. Lift the existing roll slightly to let the new egg flow underneath. When the new layer is mostly set, roll the existing log back over it, incorporating the new egg.
Repeat with the final third of egg. Cook for another 30 seconds so the outside is set and lightly golden.
Slide onto a board and leave to cool for 2 minutes. Slice into 1.5cm rounds and arrange cut-side up to show the spiral. Serve at room temperature.

items.cause: The heat was too high and the egg cooked too firmly before being rolled
items.fix: Keep the heat at the lowest possible setting and begin rolling while the surface still looks wet. A slightly underdone centre is fine as it cooks in the residual heat of the roll

items.symptom: The roll falls apart when sliced
items.cause: The roll was not tight enough or was sliced too soon after coming off the heat
items.fix: Rest the roll on a board for 2 minutes before slicing and use a sharp knife. Pressing the roll gently into a rectangular shape while it rests helps it hold together

items.symptom: The vegetables are raw and crunchy inside the omelette
items.cause: The carrot was cut too coarsely and did not cook in the short time the egg was in the pan
items.fix: Dice the carrot as finely as possible, ideally 2mm dice, or briefly blanch the carrot pieces for 1 minute before adding them to the egg

content.text: Gyeran mari is one of the three or four dishes most commonly found in a Korean packed lunchbox. Children grow up eating it alongside rice and kimchi. It is simple enough to make every morning before school and satisfying enough to feel like a proper addition to a meal. At home it also appears on the dinner table as a quick banchan when other ingredients are short. The spiral cross-section when sliced is part of its appeal, making it look carefully prepared even though it comes together in minutes.
